title: Technical guide
status: Interface and implementation guide. Export success does not prove restore or runtime behavior.

sections.title: One application interface
paragraphs: The GUI, CLI, and MCP frontends use the same application commands. Run herbert schema to read command names and schemas.
The CLI reads one UTF-8 JSON command per line from standard input. A command has schemaVersion 1, a method name and an arguments object. The CLI writes one reply per line.
Use help.read to read these documents and about to read creator details. Neither operation needs an Epicor connection. MCP exposes the same operations as help_read and about.

The public interface performs saved downloads and their lifecycle operations. Discovery occurs within a download. The interface does not provide standalone artifact browsing or example-plugin execution.

The graphical navigation starts with Connection. The other pages are Download, Plugins, and About. Connection contains the environment and authentication inputs. It also contains the credentials file picker and Save action.

Download contains the destination, output mode, Download action, and shared options. The Download action connects with the selected connection information. It does not save newly entered credentials. Plugins contains collection selection and plugin settings.

run.status adds activeOperations and executionActive to a live response. Set summary to true for compact progress. The compact response includes fileCount and fileBytes. The default response contains the full journal.

Active operations are temporary display data. Checkpoints do not save them. Continue polling while executionActive is true. Final cleanup can continue after the phase becomes completed, failed, or canceled. Saved-run reads report false. executionActive is a response field, not a journal field.

herbert mcp-config prints a Claude Desktop mcpServers entry that uses this executable and absolute local paths. Add --client codex, claude-code, gemini, vscode, cursor or generic for that client's format. It does not load state or connect.

sections.title: Errors and next steps
paragraphs: A diagnostic has code, message, retryable, an optional identity and an optional context object. Codes and field names stay stable. The message is a plain sentence that says what happened and, where Herbert knows it, what to do next.

Details such as paths, IDs, lower-level errors and server text are kept in context, not in the message. The app shows cause, osError and serverMessage under a collapsed Technical details section in error notices and run issues. MCP and CLI replies return the whole context.

On an MCP error, content[0] and structuredContent hold the full reply as before. content[1] adds plain text: the message, then a line starting Next step: when the message does not already give one. A step that asks you to save diagnostics also names the diagnostics_export tool. Successful replies have only content[0].
An invalid page size has its own message: Page size must be a whole number from 1 to 2,147,483,647, or blank to use the default. The code is INVALID_SETTING.
A refused BAQ import returns ARTIFACT_IMPORT_REFUSED. Epicor's import log is in context.serverMessage and its import decisions are in context.importDecisions.

sections.title: Connection, company and certificate trust
paragraphs: connection.test signs in, runs the Security Manager admission check, reads the companies the account can use in the same session, then signs out. It returns transportTrust and these company fields: availableCompanies, a list of {id, name}. companySource is userAccess (the account's own company access), companyList (all companies, with access confirmed when you connect) or unavailable. selectedCompany is the requested company with inList, or null when no company was given. companyListDiagnostic explains why the list could not be read, or is null.

In the app, Test connection fills the company field with the listed companies. A download needs a company. The app keeps Download disabled until one is chosen, and connection.connect without a company returns COMPANY_REQUIRED. profiles.upsert without a company saves the profile and returns the warning COMPANY_NOT_SET in warnings[]. Company membership is checked when you test or connect.

If the sign-out after a test cannot be confirmed, the error has context.connectionRetained set to true. Herbert keeps that connection only to retry the sign-out. Other operations return CONNECTION_REQUIRED with context.recoveryOperation set to connection.disconnect. Call connection.disconnect to retry the sign-out, then connect with a company.

transportTrust has mode verified (Windows trusted the certificate chain), relaxedUntrustedIssuer (the issuer was not trusted and the profile allows that) or unencrypted (plain http, so no certificate). When a certificate was observed it also has certificateSha256, subject, issuer and notAfter. These are display facts only. connection.test, connection.connect and run status report it. The run records the value at run start.

The profile option Allow self-signed certificate, field allowUntrustedCertificate, relaxes only the unknown-issuer check for that profile's connection. Normal Windows verification runs first. If only the issuer is untrusted, Herbert checks the chain again with a certificate the server presented as the anchor. A self-signed certificate or a private CA is then accepted, and the host name, the server certificate's dates, key usage and the handshake signature are still checked. capabilities.connection reports allowUntrustedCertificate and companyDiscovery support.

Limits of the option: any presented certificate can act as the anchor, so an expired intermediate certificate is not refused. Nothing is pinned, so a reconnect in the same run that presents a different certificate is accepted without notice. Use the option only for servers you control.

Certificate failures return CERTIFICATE_UNTRUSTED, CERTIFICATE_NAME_MISMATCH, CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED, CERTIFICATE_NOT_YET_VALID or CERTIFICATE_INVALID. Only CERTIFICATE_UNTRUSTED can be relaxed by the option. Revocation and signature failures return CERTIFICATE_INVALID.

sections.title: Download requests
paragraphs: Each plugin collects its inventory once, with additional pages when required. It retains full definitions from inventory pages when the service returns them.
A plugin requests each required native export once. Herbert reads the downloaded package locally to create readable code and other views.
A plugin uses separate batched reads for required content that the native export omits. System-marked artifacts remain excluded.
Herbert shares repeated reads within one run. Normal helper calls reuse the ready helper and its definition. Cleanup checks the current server object.
A failed item or inventory branch does not stop independent work. The configured retry options can repeat a failed request.
Queries that Herbert builds itself are run without being saved on the server. Their query IDs start with Herbert_, and a company filter parameter is named HerbertCompany_ followed by the table alias.

sections.title: Plugin discovery and help
paragraphs: Each Wasm module provides a descriptor with its identity, description, roles, settings and help sections. A help section has a title and an array of plain-text paragraphs.
The host discovers the modules that are present. It has no expected plugin registry. Remove a module and its state files to remove that capability.
The settings interface supplies checkboxes, choices and text filters. The module defines keys, defaults, descriptions and behavior. demoOnly marks an example option that does not affect collection.

Automation and integrations declares filterSensitiveFields. The interface label is Filter sensitive fields and parameters. Its default is false. Enabling it omits declared sensitive native fields and parameter values. System artifact exclusions apply separately. Other plugins do not inherit this setting.

Plugins own the collection choices. These choices include native methods, entity routes, projections, query tables, and native byte-field mappings. The host has no fixed allowlist for collection methods or definition tables. It checks common structure. It also requires actions to match the plugin descriptor. Authentication and ownership controls remain active.

sections.title: Portable plugin configuration
paragraphs: A plugin's state is stored beside its module. Configuration and status belong to the plugin. Keep the state file with the module when you move it.

The plugin handles configure requests. The host checks declared value shapes and saves returned opaque state. The host does not interpret a filter or assign collection meaning to a setting. Runtime status is reported by the active download.
The repository contains AssemblyScript and Rust system information examples. They demonstrate the same interface. The standard package does not contain these teaching examples.

Run pluginSettings override saved values without saving. Omission inherits saved defaults; explicit blank filters clear that run only. plugin.configure saves values. GUI category toggles, Select all available, Clear selection and Save plugin options save the draft too.

backup.start performs discovery within effective plugin options. retrieve.start uses exact native identities independently of discovery filters where acquisition is supported. The BAQs and UBAQs plugin requires paged discovery; for Functions, exact global library retrieval is supported. Processing options still apply. The persisted fullBackup discriminator controls discovery execution and does not assert full-environment coverage.

Run journals retain pluginSettings, original plugin-declared filter metadata in pluginSelectionContracts, and module fingerprints. Matching semantics belong to each module: the UD codes plugin declares ud-codes-code-type-id-prefix-v1, BAQs and UBAQs baqs-and-ubaqs-query-id-prefix-v1, and Functions functions-library-id-prefix-v1. Compact status includes frozen values, metadata and fingerprints. Recovery never borrows a missing filter from current saved options: FROZEN_SELECTION_REQUIRED refuses ambiguous legacy selection without weakening module-hash checks.

BAQs and UBAQs queryIdPrefix and Functions libraryIdPrefix are blank-default literal case-sensitive prefixes with no trimming or normalization. The BAQs and UBAQs plugin retains whole query graphs and native dependency/workflow associations. The Functions plugin passes only selected inventory IDs to bulk GetLibraries, retaining complete global libraries and company mappings. Most ID prefixes are sent to the server as a broad LIKE 'stem%' match (an OData startswith filter for Access and assignments), where the stem is the prefix up to its first %, _, [ or ] character; the exact literal check always stays local and rows outside that selection are not validated. Exceptions: Menus and launch definitions, Searches and navigation, Business rules and mappings, the Report styles and layouts stored-package path prefix and the Programs and extensions externals list read every eligible row and select locally; Kinetic applications selects locally from a light identity-only inventory and fetches content only for selected applications. Sources with no server filter (Quick, Predictive and context-menu searches, and current stored report packages) are read whole, and rows outside the selection still produce no diagnostics. Unselected families are not requested. Automation and integrations asks Epicor only for the rows its native service admits for the caller, so rows outside the caller's visibility are never downloaded. Required reference rows can name IDs outside the prefix; referenced libraries are not automatically collected. Optional compiled capture remains separate and follows selected owners.

run.status derives discoveryMessages only from successful complete overall discovery with zero selected roots. An empty page with continuation is not a zero-match result. Private filters and metadata are omitted from sanitized support packets; export performs no network calls.

sections.title: Plugin loading
paragraphs: Plugins are portable Wasm files. Loading requires a compatible plugin ABI and declared host capabilities. The standard package supplies compiled BPM, Function and UBAQ support with the matching host, modules, helper definitions and pinned native decompiler companion. Keep that composition together. Plugins require no signing key or signature file.

Herbert checks the plugin ABI and declared capabilities. Plugins in the standard package ship precompiled, so starting Herbert uses about 1 second of processor time instead of about 2 minutes. Herbert uses a precompiled module only from the plugins folder beside herbert.exe, and only when package.json binds it by SHA-256 to the exact Wasm file and to this Herbert's engine. Otherwise it compiles the Wasm itself. It reuses compiled modules while their source bytes remain unchanged. Run journals record the Wasm file's hash either way.
A plugin whose ID is a retired category code is refused at load with PLUGIN_ID_RETIRED.

sections.title: Native helpers and access ownership
paragraphs: Herbert installs and removes its server helpers through its authenticated connection. It records ownership before cleanup.

The host tracks permission checks, temporary grants when selected, helper upload, use, helper removal and permission restoration. A successful operation or a journal marked removed does not replace independent readback of server cleanup.

Connection admission requires an enabled Security Manager. Herbert checks the role once for each explicit connection. Reads and token renewal do not repeat admission. Epicor still enforces native operation permissions.

Ownership evidence must distinguish pre-existing resources from resources Herbert created. An uncertain write needs fresh readback before a retry. Remove only owned resources and preserve unrelated group memberships.

sections.title: Server changes: preview and authorization
paragraphs: New downloads use the collection method directOnly with temporary access off unless the request says otherwise. A saved GUI preference for serverAssisted is not an authorization. Direct collection that changes nothing on the server needs no authorization.

Before a run that could change the server, call serverChanges.preview with fullBackup and the run's start arguments, including a stable requestId. Preview is read-only. It returns previewId, materialDigest, materialScope, display, unresolved, authorizationRequired, readOnly and matchingAuthorizations. display shows account readiness (verified Security Manager admission, which does not itself authorize changes), the endpoint, company, caller, destination, method, temporary access, each category's helpers and native file effects, and whether server changes are possible.

To authorize, call serverChanges.authorize with previewId, materialDigest and lifetime. The lifetime is oneRun (this requestId only), session (until this Herbert connection session ends: a new connect, a disconnect or a restart) or workflow (with a workflowId you choose). expiresAt, a Unix timestamp, is optional. The result contains authorization, whose id you pass as authorizationId to backup.start or retrieve.start, and reconciled. Repeating the same acknowledgement returns the same grant. A preview with unresolved facts, a stale session or changed material facts cannot create a grant.

A run that may change the server and has no valid authorizationId is refused with SERVER_CHANGE_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED or SERVER_CHANGE_PREVIEW_REQUIRED. A grant also covers a narrower request: a longer literal prefix, fewer members, or exact identities inside its discovery scope. A changed package, company, caller or endpoint needs a new preview.

serverChanges.list and serverChanges.inspect read saved grants without contacting Epicor. serverChanges.revoke stops new optional changes at their next authorization check. Revocation, expiry or a session end never abandons resources a run already owns: cleanup of those resources keeps its original authorization. Grants are stored in the Herbert state folder. A workflow grant does not create or start a schedule.

sections.title: Server leases, cleanup and recovery
paragraphs: A run that installs temporary helpers holds a server lease. Herbert renews it every 30 seconds, and the server expires it 5 minutes after the last accepted renewal. Herbert treats the lease as lost 15 seconds before the server could expire it. A failed renewal is retried within that window. An explicit refusal, or reaching the end of the window without a confirmed renewal, marks the lease lost.

Losing the lease does not cancel the run. Herbert records SERVER_LEASE_LOST, starts no new helper work and marks affected items incomplete. Direct reads continue and cleanup still runs. A helper call that was running when the lease was lost returns SERVER_LEASE_LOST_DURING_CALL. Its result is not used and it is never retried.

At the end of a run Herbert looks for Herbert helper libraries in the run's company. It removes the helper generations this run's journal records. It also removes helpers left by an earlier Herbert version when their code matches a released Herbert helper and no running Herbert holds a live lease on them. The activity log then notes "Removed N helper(s) left on the server by an earlier Herbert version". A recognized helper under another run's live lease is kept with state active and removed by a later cleanup once that lease ends. A recognized helper found when this run has no lease host is kept with state recognized. Anything that looks like a Herbert helper but can't be confirmed, because it can't be read or its code doesn't match, is kept and reported with state unrecognized and CLEANUP_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED.

Cleanup uses only this run's own lease host and never another run's. If this run has no active host, its owned helpers stay on the server and Herbert reports SERVER_CLEANUP_PENDING. Recover the run with run.recover to finish cleanup.

run.status reports serverChanges separately from collection completeness. leaseLost is true after SERVER_LEASE_LOST. resources lists cleanup and lease outcomes with code, identity, context and outcome. This version reports uncertain for SERVER_LEASE_LOST_DURING_CALL and pending for SERVER_CLEANUP_PENDING and CLEANUP_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. The outcome schema also names noChangesObserved, removedVerified, restoredVerified, leaseReleasedSharedRemains, invokedPreexisting, failed and unknown. foreignPending lists helpers this run kept, with state active, recognized or unrecognized. They never appear in resources. Compact and full status report the same serverChanges.

sections.title: Transfer and cleanup evidence
paragraphs: Readable output uses collection display names and artifact names. If a journal lacks a collection display name, output naming falls back to its internal category ID. Herbert Data retains raw files, manifests, journals and checkpoints. Conflicts preserves incoming versions when an existing local file has changed.

Saved native responses that Herbert sanitized or scoped carry host metadata under _herbertAcquisition or _herbertRetention. Backups made by earlier versions keep their saved bytes and older key spelling. Nothing reads these keys back, and saved files are checked against their recorded hashes.

Collections use stable IDs such as ud-codes, baqs-and-ubaqs and functions. Runs, settings and backups from earlier versions are still read. Refreshing a backup made by an earlier version rewrites its Herbert Data metadata to the current IDs. That change is one-way: earlier versions cannot refresh that backup afterwards. A retired category code in an MCP or CLI request is refused with LEGACY_CATEGORY_ID, and context.replacementCategory names the current ID.
Recovery must use the durable run identity and original caller. Pending cleanup must remain visible until independent readback proves it is complete.
